statement: Lockers in a hallway are numbered $1$ to $120$. Ana puts a sticker on every locker with an even number, Ben puts a sticker on every locker whose number is a multiple of $3$, and Cara puts a sticker on every locker whose number is a multiple of $5$. How many lockers get no sticker at all?

choices.misconception: I added 60 + 40 + 24 = 124 stickered lockers, which is more than 120, so I decided every locker gets a sticker.
I subtracted the overlaps 20, 12 and 8 but forgot to add back the 4 multiples of 30, so I got 120 - 84 = 36.
I subtracted the 4 multiples of 30 again instead of adding them back, so I got 124 - 40 - 4 = 80 stickered lockers and 120 - 80 = 40.
I found the number of lockers with at least one sticker, 88, instead of the number with no sticker.

hints: A locker gets no sticker exactly when its number is not divisible by $2$, $3$ or $5$.
Use inclusion-exclusion to count the lockers with at least one sticker: add the three groups, subtract the pairs, then add back the lockers in all three groups.
At least one sticker: $60 + 40 + 24 - 20 - 12 - 8 + 4 = 88$. Subtract from $120$.

solutions.reliable: Among $1$ to $120$ there are $60$ multiples of $2$, $40$ of $3$ and $24$ of $5$. Multiples of $6$, $10$ and $15$ number $20$, $12$ and $8$, and multiples of $30$ number $4$. By inclusion-exclusion, $60 + 40 + 24 - 20 - 12 - 8 + 4 = 88$ lockers get at least one sticker, so $120 - 88 = 32$ get none.
solutions.elegant: The pattern of stickers repeats every $30$ lockers. From $1$ to $30$, the numbers divisible by none of $2$, $3$, $5$ are $1, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29$, which is $8$ numbers. Since $120 = 4 \cdot 30$, there are $4 \cdot 8 = 32$ such lockers.
